source.title: Deconstructing What Makes a Good Optimizer for Language Models
source.authors: Rosie Zhao; Depen Morwani; David Brandfonbrener; Nikhil Vyas; S. Kakade

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. Figure-only values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests optimizer-related parts of V4 and argues that Adam has no clear performance or hyperparameter-stability advantage over several alternatives in autoregressive language modeling. It does not test the claim's generalization gap on natural-label classification.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-loss and learning-rate stability results for language-model optimizer comparisons and adaptivity ablations. These bear on V4's optimizer comparison, but validation loss and stability are not held-out classification error or the train-test generalization gap. Figures supply most detailed sweep values without recoverable numbers; cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out language-model loss for Adam and momentum SGD in a new setting: C4 decoder-only transformers. Validation loss directly bears on V4's held-out-performance comparison; a classification error or train-test gap is not required. Hyperparameter stability and comparisons solely among non-SGD optimizers do not independently test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the tested setting: non-SGD optimizers have broadly comparable optimal validation performance and hyperparameter robustness, while SGD is worse. The authors' ablations identify last-layer and LayerNorm adaptivity as crucial for retaining both performance and learning-rate robustness, with some remaining benefit from adaptivity elsewhere.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer comparison and layerwise adaptivity ablations in autoregressive language-model pretraining; it reports validation loss and hyperparameter stability rather than classification train-test error gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture choices (standard versus no QK norm or z-loss) and training duration affect absolute stability; high batch size worsens validation performance; optimizer comparisons depend on optimizer and, for Lion, extreme β2 values; adaptivity allocation to last-layer and LayerNorm parameters changes performance and stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-SGD optimizers show broadly similar optimal validation loss and hyperparameter robustness; several robustness differences occur at extreme settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several alternatives to Adam match its validation performance and tuning robustness on C4 autoregressive transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation performance worsens at high batch size, but the supplied text does not establish a fixed epoch or token budget for that sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches worsen validation loss under the paper's batch-sweep protocol.

fits_no_version.finding: Layerwise and hybrid optimizer ablations identify last-layer and LayerNorm adaptivity as particularly important for performance and learning-rate robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these language models, concentrating adaptivity on selected parameter blocks recovers much of fully adaptive optimization's performance and robustness.

record.problems: The paper limits experiments to autoregressive language modeling on one dataset, fixes batch size in most experiments, and uses one-dimensional hyperparameter sweeps that may miss interactions. Most sweep values are shown only in figures, without numeric values in the supplied text. Results use validation loss and learning-rate stability, not the classification train-test error gap in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Cited prior-work comparisons and mathematical discussion without new measurements were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

Image benchmarks; training-performance comparisons; controlled limited-versus-broader tuning comparisons; decoupled-weight-decay recovery; switching from Adam to SGD; the specific word-level language-model exception. The study uses one-dimensional sweeps rather than an exhaustive tuning comparison.
Batch-size effects under an established fixed epoch or token budget, and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout's held-out-error effects and its interaction with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings and their correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure captions and prose explicitly establish the relevant rankings despite unavailable numerical curve values. Stability alone cannot establish V4. No fixed-epoch batch-size verdict is justified by the supplied protocol.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.

Image-classification benchmarks; comparisons specifically under limited tuning of learning rates and decay schedules; equal or better training performance; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay and Adam-to-SGD switching; word-level language-model exception.
Large-batch penalty under fixed epoch budgets and the cited recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the classification train-test gap.
Removing highly memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
